about.title: About & Clinical Safety
about.p1: NeuroSathi is a low-cost brain-health monitoring and care-linkage platform engineered specifically for low-income and rural patients living with neurological conditions (multiple sclerosis, epilepsy, stroke follow-up).
about.p2: Built for the Seva First Innovation Challenge (SFIC) by DTU, it bridges the vast neurologist gap in India through accessible mobile surveillance and ASHA/CHW integration.
about.privacyP1: All data stays strictly on your device (in browser localStorage). No external cloud database or account is required.
about.privacyP2: Designed in alignment with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA), 2023 principles.
about.lim1: Assessments are clinically inspired but not yet validated in a formal clinical trial.
about.lim2: Speech assessment records duration only — NLP acoustic analysis is not implemented in this prototype.
about.lim3: Government scheme integration is simulated with links — live API integration is planned for the pilot.
about.lim4: Hospital directory uses sample regional centers — real-time directory integration is in progress.
about.lim5: Decline detection threshold is a configurable starting point, not an absolute clinical cutoff.
about.impact1: Target: Rural and semi-urban patients with scarce neurological access.
about.impact2: Cost: ₹0 to patient. Works offline on budget Android phones without paid APIs.
about.impact3: Comparison: Unlike expensive urban consultation apps, NeuroSathi is free, offline-ready, multi-lingual, and designed for grassroots health workers.
about.phase1: Phase 1 (Current): Functional web prototype with sample data — TRL 3
about.phase2: Phase 2 (75 Days): Pilot with 50 patients across 2 PHCs in Telangana & Delhi, validate with neurologists, connect hospital directories
about.phase3: Phase 3 (6 Months): Clinical validation study, WhatsApp bot for CHW alerts, e-Sanjeevani API linkage
about.phase4: Phase 4 (1 Year): National Health Mission (NHM) integration proposal, scaling to 5 states
about.teamPlaceholder: DTU Innovation Team & MBBS Clinical Advisor
about.viksitBharat: Built for Viksit Bharat — affordable neurological care monitoring for every Indian 🇮🇳

emergency.title: Emergency Red Flags
emergency.subtitle: When to seek urgent and immediate emergency medical care
emergency.strokeDesc: Stroke is a medical emergency. Use FAST to identify symptoms immediately:
emergency.faceQ: FACE: Ask the person to smile. Does one side of the face droop?
emergency.armsQ: ARMS: Ask them to raise both arms. Does one arm drift downward?
emergency.speechQ: SPEECH: Ask them to repeat a simple phrase. Is speech slurred or strange?
emergency.timeQ: TIME: If ANY of these are YES — this is an emergency. Call 108 NOW.
emergency.inst1: Note the exact time symptoms started — tell the doctor immediately
emergency.inst2: Do NOT give food or water (choking risk)
emergency.inst3: Do NOT give aspirin unless specifically instructed by a doctor
emergency.inst4: Lay the person on their side if they feel sick or vomit
emergency.inst5: Keep them calm, warm, and still until the ambulance arrives
emergency.goldenHour: Golden Hour: Emergency intervention within 4.5 hours can prevent permanent brain damage.
emergency.strokeNormal: No stroke warning signs reported currently. Stay watchful. If any sign appears, return to this screen immediately.
emergency.seizureEmergTitle: ⚡ When a Seizure Needs Emergency Care
emergency.seizureEmergDesc: Most seizures end on their own. Call 108 immediately if any of these occur:
emergency.seizCrit2: Person does not wake up after the seizure
emergency.seizCrit3: A second seizure follows quickly without regaining consciousness
emergency.seizCrit4: Person is injured, in water, or pregnant
emergency.seizCrit5: This is their FIRST seizure ever
emergency.seizCrit6: Person has difficulty breathing or blue lips after the seizure
emergency.seizureFirstAidTitle: SEIZURE FIRST AID — What to do RIGHT NOW
emergency.do1: Clear the area of sharp or hard objects
emergency.do2: Place something soft (cloth/pillow) under their head
emergency.do3: Turn them gently onto their side (recovery position)
emergency.do4: Time the seizure with a watch or phone
emergency.do5: Stay with them reassuringly until fully awake
emergency.dont1: Do NOT put anything in their mouth (no spoons, keys, water)
emergency.dont2: Do NOT hold them down or restrain their movements
emergency.dont3: Do NOT give water, food, or medicines until fully awake
emergency.dont4: Do NOT panic — most seizures stop within 1 to 3 minutes
emergency.msRelapseTitle: 🔶 Signs of an MS Relapse — When to Contact Your Doctor
emergency.msRelapseDesc: A relapse refers to new symptoms or significant worsening of existing symptoms lasting more than 24 hours without fever:
emergency.msSign1: New numbness or tingling lasting more than 24 hours
emergency.msSign2: Sudden vision problems — blurring, double vision, or eye pain
emergency.msSign3: Severe new weakness in legs or arms making walking difficult
emergency.msSign4: Loss of balance or inability to walk that is new
emergency.msSign5: Bladder problems that are sudden and new
emergency.msRelapseMsg: Contact your neurologist or Primary Health Centre doctor promptly.
emergency.dangerDesc: Proceed to the nearest emergency department if you experience:
emergency.danger1: Sudden severe headache (worst headache of your life)
emergency.danger2: Sudden confusion or inability to understand speech
emergency.danger3: Sudden loss of vision in one or both eyes
emergency.danger4: Sudden weakness or numbness on one side of the body

clinicalScales.title: Clinical Functional Scales

clinicalScales.mrsDesc: Measures degree of daily disability or dependence after stroke (0 = No symptoms, 5 = Severe disability):
clinicalScales.mrs0: 0 — No problems at all. I can do everything I did before stroke.
clinicalScales.mrs1: 1 — Minor difficulties, but I can do all my usual activities without help.
clinicalScales.mrs2: 2 — I cannot do some prior activities, but look after myself independently.
clinicalScales.mrs3: 3 — I need some assistance, but I am able to walk without another person.
clinicalScales.mrs4: 4 — I cannot walk or attend to body care needs without assistance.
clinicalScales.mrs5: 5 — Bedridden, incontinent, and requiring constant nursing care.
clinicalScales.edssDesc: Evaluates 6 functional domains on a 1 (severe difficulty) to 5 (normal) scale:
clinicalScales.seizQ1: How much do seizures affect your ability to work, study, or farm?
clinicalScales.seizQ2: How much do seizures affect your social life and community interactions?

clinicalScales.seizQ4: How well controlled do you feel your seizures are on current medicines?
clinicalScales.seizQ5: How much do medicine side effects affect your everyday wellbeing?

caregiver.title: Caregiver & Family Guide
caregiver.subtitle: Practical training, emergency guidance, home rehabilitation, and nutrition
caregiver.rehabStroke1: Hand Ball Squeezes: Squeeze a soft rubber ball 10 times with each hand, 3 sets daily.
caregiver.rehabStroke2: Supported Arm Raises: Slowly lift both arms overhead for 5 seconds. Repeat 10 times.
caregiver.rehabStroke3: Ankle Circles: Rotate ankles in circles 10 times each direction while seated.
caregiver.rehabStroke4: Chair Sit-to-Stand: Stand up slowly without pulling, pause, and sit down gently. 5-10 times.
caregiver.rehabStroke5: Guided Walking: Walk slowly with a cane or family support, aiming for small daily increases.
caregiver.rehabMsTitle: Safe Daily Movement for Multiple Sclerosis
caregiver.rehabMs1: Gentle Stretching: Full-body stretching 5-10 minutes each morning to reduce stiffness.
caregiver.rehabMs2: Wall-Supported Balance: Stand near a sturdy wall; raise one foot for 10 seconds. Switch sides.
caregiver.rehabMs3: Cooling Precautions: Exercise in ventilated cool areas. Stop if feeling overheated.
caregiver.rehabMs4: Energy Pacing: Rest proactively. Do not push through severe neurological fatigue.
caregiver.rehabEpilepsy1: Consistent Sleep Schedule: Go to bed and wake up at consistent times every day.
caregiver.rehabEpilepsy2: Stress Reduction: 5 minutes of slow diaphragmatic breathing when feeling overwhelmed.
caregiver.rehabEpilepsy3: Exercise with a Buddy: Exercise with family nearby; avoid swimming or climbing alone.
caregiver.nutri1: Omega-3 Healthy Fats: Flaxseeds (Alsi) ground in roti, mustard oil in cooking, walnuts (akhrot).
caregiver.nutri2: Iron & Energy: Spinach (Palak), Jaggery (Gur), Ragi porridge, dates (Khajoor).
caregiver.nutri3: Nerve Health (B12): Fresh milk, homemade curd (Dahi), eggs, paneer.
caregiver.nutri4: Antioxidants: Turmeric (Haldi) with warm milk, amla, tomatoes, carrots.
caregiver.nutri5: Hydration: Drink 8-10 glasses of clean water daily. Avoid excess strong chai or alcohol.

emergency.title: आपातकालीन चेतावनी संकेत (रेड फ्लैग)
emergency.subtitle: When to seek urgent and immediate emergency medical care
emergency.strokeDesc: Stroke is a medical emergency. Use FAST to identify symptoms immediately:
emergency.faceQ: FACE: Ask the person to smile. Does one side of the face droop?
emergency.armsQ: ARMS: Ask them to raise both arms. Does one arm drift downward?
emergency.speechQ: SPEECH: Ask them to repeat a simple phrase. Is speech slurred or strange?
emergency.timeQ: TIME: If ANY of these are YES — this is an emergency. Call 108 NOW.
emergency.inst1: Note the exact time symptoms started — tell the doctor immediately
emergency.inst2: Do NOT give food or water (choking risk)
emergency.inst3: Do NOT give aspirin unless specifically instructed by a doctor
emergency.inst4: Lay the person on their side if they feel sick or vomit
emergency.inst5: Keep them calm, warm, and still until the ambulance arrives
emergency.goldenHour: Golden Hour: Emergency intervention within 4.5 hours can prevent permanent brain damage.
emergency.strokeNormal: No stroke warning signs reported currently. Stay watchful. If any sign appears, return to this screen immediately.
emergency.seizureEmergTitle: ⚡ When a Seizure Needs Emergency Care
emergency.seizureEmergDesc: Most seizures end on their own. Call 108 immediately if any of these occur:
emergency.seizCrit2: Person does not wake up after the seizure
emergency.seizCrit3: A second seizure follows quickly without regaining consciousness
emergency.seizCrit4: Person is injured, in water, or pregnant
emergency.seizCrit5: This is their FIRST seizure ever
emergency.seizCrit6: Person has difficulty breathing or blue lips after the seizure
emergency.seizureFirstAidTitle: SEIZURE FIRST AID — What to do RIGHT NOW
emergency.do1: Clear the area of sharp or hard objects
emergency.do2: Place something soft (cloth/pillow) under their head
emergency.do3: Turn them gently onto their side (recovery position)
emergency.do4: Time the seizure with a watch or phone
emergency.do5: Stay with them reassuringly until fully awake
emergency.dont1: Do NOT put anything in their mouth (no spoons, keys, water)
emergency.dont2: Do NOT hold them down or restrain their movements
emergency.dont3: Do NOT give water, food, or medicines until fully awake
emergency.dont4: Do NOT panic — most seizures stop within 1 to 3 minutes
emergency.msRelapseTitle: 🔶 Signs of an MS Relapse — When to Contact Your Doctor
emergency.msRelapseDesc: A relapse refers to new symptoms or significant worsening of existing symptoms lasting more than 24 hours without fever:
emergency.msSign1: New numbness or tingling lasting more than 24 hours
emergency.msSign2: Sudden vision problems — blurring, double vision, or eye pain
emergency.msSign3: Severe new weakness in legs or arms making walking difficult
emergency.msSign4: Loss of balance or inability to walk that is new
emergency.msSign5: Bladder problems that are sudden and new
emergency.msRelapseMsg: Contact your neurologist or Primary Health Centre doctor promptly.
emergency.dangerDesc: Proceed to the nearest emergency department if you experience:
emergency.danger1: Sudden severe headache (worst headache of your life)
emergency.danger2: Sudden confusion or inability to understand speech
emergency.danger3: Sudden loss of vision in one or both eyes
emergency.danger4: Sudden weakness or numbness on one side of the body

clinicalScales.title: नैदानिक कार्यात्मक मापदंड
clinicalScales.subtitle: Standardized clinician-aligned functional evaluations for longitudinal monitoring
clinicalScales.mrsDesc: Measures degree of daily disability or dependence after stroke (0 = No symptoms, 5 = Severe disability):
clinicalScales.mrs0: 0 — No problems at all. I can do everything I did before stroke.
clinicalScales.mrs1: 1 — Minor difficulties, but I can do all my usual activities without help.
clinicalScales.mrs2: 2 — I cannot do some prior activities, but look after myself independently.
clinicalScales.mrs3: 3 — I need some assistance, but I am able to walk without another person.
clinicalScales.mrs4: 4 — I cannot walk or attend to body care needs without assistance.
clinicalScales.mrs5: 5 — Bedridden, incontinent, and requiring constant nursing care.
clinicalScales.edssDesc: Evaluates 6 functional domains on a 1 (severe difficulty) to 5 (normal) scale:
clinicalScales.seizQ1: How much do seizures affect your ability to work, study, or farm?
clinicalScales.seizQ2: How much do seizures affect your social life and community interactions?
clinicalScales.seizQ3: How worried are you about having a seizure in public places?

caregiver.title: देखभालकर्ता एवं परिवार मार्गदर्शिका
caregiver.subtitle: Practical training, emergency guidance, home rehabilitation, and nutrition
caregiver.rehabStroke1: Hand Ball Squeezes: Squeeze a soft rubber ball 10 times with each hand, 3 sets daily.
caregiver.rehabStroke2: Supported Arm Raises: Slowly lift both arms overhead for 5 seconds. Repeat 10 times.
caregiver.rehabStroke3: Ankle Circles: Rotate ankles in circles 10 times each direction while seated.
caregiver.rehabStroke4: Chair Sit-to-Stand: Stand up slowly without pulling, pause, and sit down gently. 5-10 times.
caregiver.rehabStroke5: Guided Walking: Walk slowly with a cane or family support, aiming for small daily increases.
caregiver.rehabMsTitle: Safe Daily Movement for Multiple Sclerosis
caregiver.rehabMs1: Gentle Stretching: Full-body stretching 5-10 minutes each morning to reduce stiffness.
caregiver.rehabMs2: Wall-Supported Balance: Stand near a sturdy wall; raise one foot for 10 seconds. Switch sides.
caregiver.rehabMs3: Cooling Precautions: Exercise in ventilated cool areas. Stop if feeling overheated.
caregiver.rehabMs4: Energy Pacing: Rest proactively. Do not push through severe neurological fatigue.
caregiver.rehabEpilepsy1: Consistent Sleep Schedule: Go to bed and wake up at consistent times every day.
caregiver.rehabEpilepsy2: Stress Reduction: 5 minutes of slow diaphragmatic breathing when feeling overwhelmed.
caregiver.rehabEpilepsy3: Exercise with a Buddy: Exercise with family nearby; avoid swimming or climbing alone.
caregiver.nutri1: Omega-3 Healthy Fats: Flaxseeds (Alsi) ground in roti, mustard oil in cooking, walnuts (akhrot).
caregiver.nutri2: Iron & Energy: Spinach (Palak), Jaggery (Gur), Ragi porridge, dates (Khajoor).
caregiver.nutri3: Nerve Health (B12): Fresh milk, homemade curd (Dahi), eggs, paneer.
caregiver.nutri4: Antioxidants: Turmeric (Haldi) with warm milk, amla, tomatoes, carrots.
caregiver.nutri5: Hydration: Drink 8-10 glasses of clean water daily. Avoid excess strong chai or alcohol.

emergency.title: అత్యవసర హెచ్చరిక సంకేతాలు (రెడ్ ఫ్లాగ్స్)
emergency.subtitle: When to seek urgent and immediate emergency medical care
emergency.strokeDesc: Stroke is a medical emergency. Use FAST to identify symptoms immediately:
emergency.faceQ: FACE: Ask the person to smile. Does one side of the face droop?
emergency.armsQ: ARMS: Ask them to raise both arms. Does one arm drift downward?
emergency.speechQ: SPEECH: Ask them to repeat a simple phrase. Is speech slurred or strange?
emergency.timeQ: TIME: If ANY of these are YES — this is an emergency. Call 108 NOW.
emergency.inst1: Note the exact time symptoms started — tell the doctor immediately
emergency.inst2: Do NOT give food or water (choking risk)
emergency.inst3: Do NOT give aspirin unless specifically instructed by a doctor
emergency.inst4: Lay the person on their side if they feel sick or vomit
emergency.inst5: Keep them calm, warm, and still until the ambulance arrives
emergency.goldenHour: Golden Hour: Emergency intervention within 4.5 hours can prevent permanent brain damage.
emergency.strokeNormal: No stroke warning signs reported currently. Stay watchful. If any sign appears, return to this screen immediately.
emergency.seizureEmergTitle: ⚡ When a Seizure Needs Emergency Care
emergency.seizureEmergDesc: Most seizures end on their own. Call 108 immediately if any of these occur:
emergency.seizCrit2: Person does not wake up after the seizure
emergency.seizCrit3: A second seizure follows quickly without regaining consciousness
emergency.seizCrit4: Person is injured, in water, or pregnant
emergency.seizCrit5: This is their FIRST seizure ever
emergency.seizCrit6: Person has difficulty breathing or blue lips after the seizure
emergency.seizureFirstAidTitle: SEIZURE FIRST AID — What to do RIGHT NOW
emergency.do1: Clear the area of sharp or hard objects
emergency.do2: Place something soft (cloth/pillow) under their head
emergency.do3: Turn them gently onto their side (recovery position)
emergency.do4: Time the seizure with a watch or phone
emergency.do5: Stay with them reassuringly until fully awake
emergency.dont1: Do NOT put anything in their mouth (no spoons, keys, water)
emergency.dont2: Do NOT hold them down or restrain their movements
emergency.dont3: Do NOT give water, food, or medicines until fully awake
emergency.dont4: Do NOT panic — most seizures stop within 1 to 3 minutes
emergency.msRelapseTitle: 🔶 Signs of an MS Relapse — When to Contact Your Doctor
emergency.msRelapseDesc: A relapse refers to new symptoms or significant worsening of existing symptoms lasting more than 24 hours without fever:
emergency.msSign1: New numbness or tingling lasting more than 24 hours
emergency.msSign2: Sudden vision problems — blurring, double vision, or eye pain
emergency.msSign3: Severe new weakness in legs or arms making walking difficult
emergency.msSign4: Loss of balance or inability to walk that is new
emergency.msSign5: Bladder problems that are sudden and new
emergency.msRelapseMsg: Contact your neurologist or Primary Health Centre doctor promptly.
emergency.dangerDesc: Proceed to the nearest emergency department if you experience:
emergency.danger1: Sudden severe headache (worst headache of your life)
emergency.danger2: Sudden confusion or inability to understand speech
emergency.danger3: Sudden loss of vision in one or both eyes
emergency.danger4: Sudden weakness or numbness on one side of the body

clinicalScales.subtitle: Standardized clinician-aligned functional evaluations for longitudinal monitoring
clinicalScales.mrsDesc: Measures degree of daily disability or dependence after stroke (0 = No symptoms, 5 = Severe disability):
clinicalScales.mrs0: 0 — No problems at all. I can do everything I did before stroke.
clinicalScales.mrs1: 1 — Minor difficulties, but I can do all my usual activities without help.
clinicalScales.mrs2: 2 — I cannot do some prior activities, but look after myself independently.
clinicalScales.mrs3: 3 — I need some assistance, but I am able to walk without another person.
clinicalScales.mrs4: 4 — I cannot walk or attend to body care needs without assistance.
clinicalScales.mrs5: 5 — Bedridden, incontinent, and requiring constant nursing care.
clinicalScales.edssDesc: Evaluates 6 functional domains on a 1 (severe difficulty) to 5 (normal) scale:
clinicalScales.seizQ1: How much do seizures affect your ability to work, study, or farm?
clinicalScales.seizQ2: How much do seizures affect your social life and community interactions?
clinicalScales.seizQ3: How worried are you about having a seizure in public places?
clinicalScales.seizQ4: How well controlled do you feel your seizures are on current medicines?
clinicalScales.seizQ5: How much do medicine side effects affect your everyday wellbeing?

caregiver.subtitle: Practical training, emergency guidance, home rehabilitation, and nutrition
caregiver.rehabStroke1: Hand Ball Squeezes: Squeeze a soft rubber ball 10 times with each hand, 3 sets daily.
caregiver.rehabStroke2: Supported Arm Raises: Slowly lift both arms overhead for 5 seconds. Repeat 10 times.
caregiver.rehabStroke3: Ankle Circles: Rotate ankles in circles 10 times each direction while seated.
caregiver.rehabStroke4: Chair Sit-to-Stand: Stand up slowly without pulling, pause, and sit down gently. 5-10 times.
caregiver.rehabStroke5: Guided Walking: Walk slowly with a cane or family support, aiming for small daily increases.
caregiver.rehabMsTitle: Safe Daily Movement for Multiple Sclerosis
caregiver.rehabMs1: Gentle Stretching: Full-body stretching 5-10 minutes each morning to reduce stiffness.
caregiver.rehabMs2: Wall-Supported Balance: Stand near a sturdy wall; raise one foot for 10 seconds. Switch sides.
caregiver.rehabMs3: Cooling Precautions: Exercise in ventilated cool areas. Stop if feeling overheated.
caregiver.rehabMs4: Energy Pacing: Rest proactively. Do not push through severe neurological fatigue.
caregiver.rehabEpilepsy1: Consistent Sleep Schedule: Go to bed and wake up at consistent times every day.
caregiver.rehabEpilepsy2: Stress Reduction: 5 minutes of slow diaphragmatic breathing when feeling overwhelmed.
caregiver.rehabEpilepsy3: Exercise with a Buddy: Exercise with family nearby; avoid swimming or climbing alone.
caregiver.nutri1: Omega-3 Healthy Fats: Flaxseeds (Alsi) ground in roti, mustard oil in cooking, walnuts (akhrot).
caregiver.nutri2: Iron & Energy: Spinach (Palak), Jaggery (Gur), Ragi porridge, dates (Khajoor).
caregiver.nutri3: Nerve Health (B12): Fresh milk, homemade curd (Dahi), eggs, paneer.
caregiver.nutri4: Antioxidants: Turmeric (Haldi) with warm milk, amla, tomatoes, carrots.
caregiver.nutri5: Hydration: Drink 8-10 glasses of clean water daily. Avoid excess strong chai or alcohol.
caregiver.phqDesc: Over the past 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by any of the following problems?
caregiver.phqQ1: 1. Little interest or pleasure in doing things
caregiver.phqPositive: Your responses suggest you may benefit from speaking with a counselor. This is common and treatable. Please call Tele-MANAS (14416) or talk to your doctor.
caregiver.phqNegative: Screening score is within the normal range. Continue regular wellness practices.

emergency.title: ہنگامی خطرے کی علامات (ریڈ فلیگز)
emergency.subtitle: When to seek urgent and immediate emergency medical care
emergency.strokeDesc: Stroke is a medical emergency. Use FAST to identify symptoms immediately:
emergency.faceQ: FACE: Ask the person to smile. Does one side of the face droop?
emergency.armsQ: ARMS: Ask them to raise both arms. Does one arm drift downward?
emergency.speechQ: SPEECH: Ask them to repeat a simple phrase. Is speech slurred or strange?
emergency.timeQ: TIME: If ANY of these are YES — this is an emergency. Call 108 NOW.
emergency.call108: فوری طور پر 108 ایمبولینس کو کال کریں
emergency.inst1: Note the exact time symptoms started — tell the doctor immediately
emergency.inst2: Do NOT give food or water (choking risk)
emergency.inst3: Do NOT give aspirin unless specifically instructed by a doctor
emergency.inst4: Lay the person on their side if they feel sick or vomit
emergency.inst5: Keep them calm, warm, and still until the ambulance arrives
emergency.goldenHour: Golden Hour: Emergency intervention within 4.5 hours can prevent permanent brain damage.
emergency.strokeNormal: No stroke warning signs reported currently. Stay watchful. If any sign appears, return to this screen immediately.
emergency.seizureEmergTitle: ⚡ When a Seizure Needs Emergency Care
emergency.seizureEmergDesc: Most seizures end on their own. Call 108 immediately if any of these occur:
emergency.seizCrit2: Person does not wake up after the seizure
emergency.seizCrit3: A second seizure follows quickly without regaining consciousness
emergency.seizCrit4: Person is injured, in water, or pregnant
emergency.seizCrit5: This is their FIRST seizure ever
emergency.seizCrit6: Person has difficulty breathing or blue lips after the seizure
emergency.seizureFirstAidTitle: SEIZURE FIRST AID — What to do RIGHT NOW
emergency.do1: Clear the area of sharp or hard objects
emergency.do2: Place something soft (cloth/pillow) under their head
emergency.do3: Turn them gently onto their side (recovery position)
emergency.do4: Time the seizure with a watch or phone
emergency.do5: Stay with them reassuringly until fully awake
emergency.dont1: Do NOT put anything in their mouth (no spoons, keys, water)
emergency.dont2: Do NOT hold them down or restrain their movements
emergency.dont3: Do NOT give water, food, or medicines until fully awake
emergency.dont4: Do NOT panic — most seizures stop within 1 to 3 minutes
emergency.msRelapseTitle: 🔶 Signs of an MS Relapse — When to Contact Your Doctor
emergency.msRelapseDesc: A relapse refers to new symptoms or significant worsening of existing symptoms lasting more than 24 hours without fever:
emergency.msSign1: New numbness or tingling lasting more than 24 hours
emergency.msSign2: Sudden vision problems — blurring, double vision, or eye pain
emergency.msSign3: Severe new weakness in legs or arms making walking difficult
emergency.msSign4: Loss of balance or inability to walk that is new
emergency.msSign5: Bladder problems that are sudden and new
emergency.msRelapseMsg: Contact your neurologist or Primary Health Centre doctor promptly.
emergency.dangerDesc: Proceed to the nearest emergency department if you experience:
emergency.danger1: Sudden severe headache (worst headache of your life)
emergency.danger2: Sudden confusion or inability to understand speech
emergency.danger3: Sudden loss of vision in one or both eyes
emergency.danger4: Sudden weakness or numbness on one side of the body

clinicalScales.mrsDesc: Measures degree of daily disability or dependence after stroke (0 = No symptoms, 5 = Severe disability):
clinicalScales.mrs0: 0 — No problems at all. I can do everything I did before stroke.
clinicalScales.mrs1: 1 — Minor difficulties, but I can do all my usual activities without help.
clinicalScales.mrs2: 2 — I cannot do some prior activities, but look after myself independently.
clinicalScales.mrs3: 3 — I need some assistance, but I am able to walk without another person.
clinicalScales.mrs4: 4 — I cannot walk or attend to body care needs without assistance.
clinicalScales.mrs5: 5 — Bedridden, incontinent, and requiring constant nursing care.

clinicalScales.seizQ1: How much do seizures affect your ability to work, study, or farm?

caregiver.title: دیکھ بھال کرنے والوں کی رہنمائی
caregiver.subtitle: Practical training, emergency guidance, home rehabilitation, and nutrition
caregiver.rehabStroke1: Hand Ball Squeezes: Squeeze a soft rubber ball 10 times with each hand, 3 sets daily.
caregiver.rehabStroke2: Supported Arm Raises: Slowly lift both arms overhead for 5 seconds. Repeat 10 times.
caregiver.rehabStroke3: Ankle Circles: Rotate ankles in circles 10 times each direction while seated.
caregiver.rehabStroke4: Chair Sit-to-Stand: Stand up slowly without pulling, pause, and sit down gently. 5-10 times.
caregiver.rehabStroke5: Guided Walking: Walk slowly with a cane or family support, aiming for small daily increases.
caregiver.rehabMsTitle: Safe Daily Movement for Multiple Sclerosis
caregiver.rehabMs1: Gentle Stretching: Full-body stretching 5-10 minutes each morning to reduce stiffness.
caregiver.rehabMs2: Wall-Supported Balance: Stand near a sturdy wall; raise one foot for 10 seconds. Switch sides.
caregiver.rehabMs3: Cooling Precautions: Exercise in ventilated cool areas. Stop if feeling overheated.
caregiver.rehabMs4: Energy Pacing: Rest proactively. Do not push through severe neurological fatigue.
caregiver.rehabEpilepsy1: Consistent Sleep Schedule: Go to bed and wake up at consistent times every day.
caregiver.rehabEpilepsy2: Stress Reduction: 5 minutes of slow diaphragmatic breathing when feeling overwhelmed.
caregiver.rehabEpilepsy3: Exercise with a Buddy: Exercise with family nearby; avoid swimming or climbing alone.
caregiver.nutri1: Omega-3 Healthy Fats: Flaxseeds (Alsi) ground in roti, mustard oil in cooking, walnuts (akhrot).
caregiver.nutri2: Iron & Energy: Spinach (Palak), Jaggery (Gur), Ragi porridge, dates (Khajoor).
caregiver.nutri3: Nerve Health (B12): Fresh milk, homemade curd (Dahi), eggs, paneer.
caregiver.nutri4: Antioxidants: Turmeric (Haldi) with warm milk, amla, tomatoes, carrots.
caregiver.nutri5: Hydration: Drink 8-10 glasses of clean water daily. Avoid excess strong chai or alcohol.

emergency.title: आपातकालीन चेतावनी संकेत (रेड फ्लैग)
emergency.subtitle: When to seek urgent and immediate emergency medical care
emergency.strokeDesc: Stroke is a medical emergency. Use FAST to identify symptoms immediately:
emergency.faceQ: FACE: Ask the person to smile. Does one side of the face droop?
emergency.armsQ: ARMS: Ask them to raise both arms. Does one arm drift downward?
emergency.speechQ: SPEECH: Ask them to repeat a simple phrase. Is speech slurred or strange?
emergency.timeQ: TIME: If ANY of these are YES — this is an emergency. Call 108 NOW.
emergency.inst1: Note the exact time symptoms started — tell the doctor immediately
emergency.inst2: Do NOT give food or water (choking risk)
emergency.inst3: Do NOT give aspirin unless specifically instructed by a doctor
emergency.inst4: Lay the person on their side if they feel sick or vomit
emergency.inst5: Keep them calm, warm, and still until the ambulance arrives
emergency.goldenHour: Golden Hour: Emergency intervention within 4.5 hours can prevent permanent brain damage.
emergency.strokeNormal: No stroke warning signs reported currently. Stay watchful. If any sign appears, return to this screen immediately.
emergency.seizureEmergTitle: ⚡ When a Seizure Needs Emergency Care
emergency.seizureEmergDesc: Most seizures end on their own. Call 108 immediately if any of these occur:
emergency.seizCrit2: Person does not wake up after the seizure
emergency.seizCrit3: A second seizure follows quickly without regaining consciousness
emergency.seizCrit4: Person is injured, in water, or pregnant
emergency.seizCrit5: This is their FIRST seizure ever
emergency.seizCrit6: Person has difficulty breathing or blue lips after the seizure
emergency.seizureFirstAidTitle: SEIZURE FIRST AID — What to do RIGHT NOW
emergency.do1: Clear the area of sharp or hard objects
emergency.do2: Place something soft (cloth/pillow) under their head
emergency.do3: Turn them gently onto their side (recovery position)
emergency.do4: Time the seizure with a watch or phone
emergency.do5: Stay with them reassuringly until fully awake
emergency.dont1: Do NOT put anything in their mouth (no spoons, keys, water)
emergency.dont2: Do NOT hold them down or restrain their movements
emergency.dont3: Do NOT give water, food, or medicines until fully awake
emergency.dont4: Do NOT panic — most seizures stop within 1 to 3 minutes
emergency.msRelapseTitle: 🔶 Signs of an MS Relapse — When to Contact Your Doctor
emergency.msRelapseDesc: A relapse refers to new symptoms or significant worsening of existing symptoms lasting more than 24 hours without fever:
emergency.msSign1: New numbness or tingling lasting more than 24 hours
emergency.msSign2: Sudden vision problems — blurring, double vision, or eye pain
emergency.msSign3: Severe new weakness in legs or arms making walking difficult
emergency.msSign4: Loss of balance or inability to walk that is new
emergency.msSign5: Bladder problems that are sudden and new
emergency.msRelapseMsg: Contact your neurologist or Primary Health Centre doctor promptly.
emergency.dangerDesc: Proceed to the nearest emergency department if you experience:
emergency.danger1: Sudden severe headache (worst headache of your life)
emergency.danger2: Sudden confusion or inability to understand speech
emergency.danger3: Sudden loss of vision in one or both eyes
emergency.danger4: Sudden weakness or numbness on one side of the body

clinicalScales.title: नैदानिक कार्यात्मक मापदंड
clinicalScales.subtitle: Standardized clinician-aligned functional evaluations for longitudinal monitoring
clinicalScales.mrsDesc: Measures degree of daily disability or dependence after stroke (0 = No symptoms, 5 = Severe disability):
clinicalScales.mrs0: 0 — No problems at all. I can do everything I did before stroke.
clinicalScales.mrs1: 1 — Minor difficulties, but I can do all my usual activities without help.
clinicalScales.mrs2: 2 — I cannot do some prior activities, but look after myself independently.
clinicalScales.mrs3: 3 — I need some assistance, but I am able to walk without another person.
clinicalScales.mrs4: 4 — I cannot walk or attend to body care needs without assistance.
clinicalScales.mrs5: 5 — Bedridden, incontinent, and requiring constant nursing care.
clinicalScales.edssDesc: Evaluates 6 functional domains on a 1 (severe difficulty) to 5 (normal) scale:
clinicalScales.seizQ1: How much do seizures affect your ability to work, study, or farm?
clinicalScales.seizQ2: How much do seizures affect your social life and community interactions?
clinicalScales.seizQ3: How worried are you about having a seizure in public places?
clinicalScales.seizQ4: How well controlled do you feel your seizures are on current medicines?
clinicalScales.seizQ5: How much do medicine side effects affect your everyday wellbeing?

caregiver.subtitle: Practical training, emergency guidance, home rehabilitation, and nutrition
caregiver.rehabStroke1: Hand Ball Squeezes: Squeeze a soft rubber ball 10 times with each hand, 3 sets daily.
caregiver.rehabStroke2: Supported Arm Raises: Slowly lift both arms overhead for 5 seconds. Repeat 10 times.
caregiver.rehabStroke3: Ankle Circles: Rotate ankles in circles 10 times each direction while seated.
caregiver.rehabStroke4: Chair Sit-to-Stand: Stand up slowly without pulling, pause, and sit down gently. 5-10 times.
caregiver.rehabStroke5: Guided Walking: Walk slowly with a cane or family support, aiming for small daily increases.
caregiver.rehabMsTitle: Safe Daily Movement for Multiple Sclerosis
caregiver.rehabMs1: Gentle Stretching: Full-body stretching 5-10 minutes each morning to reduce stiffness.
caregiver.rehabMs2: Wall-Supported Balance: Stand near a sturdy wall; raise one foot for 10 seconds. Switch sides.
caregiver.rehabMs3: Cooling Precautions: Exercise in ventilated cool areas. Stop if feeling overheated.
caregiver.rehabMs4: Energy Pacing: Rest proactively. Do not push through severe neurological fatigue.
caregiver.rehabEpilepsy1: Consistent Sleep Schedule: Go to bed and wake up at consistent times every day.
caregiver.rehabEpilepsy2: Stress Reduction: 5 minutes of slow diaphragmatic breathing when feeling overwhelmed.
caregiver.rehabEpilepsy3: Exercise with a Buddy: Exercise with family nearby; avoid swimming or climbing alone.
caregiver.nutri1: Omega-3 Healthy Fats: Flaxseeds (Alsi) ground in roti, mustard oil in cooking, walnuts (akhrot).
caregiver.nutri2: Iron & Energy: Spinach (Palak), Jaggery (Gur), Ragi porridge, dates (Khajoor).
caregiver.nutri3: Nerve Health (B12): Fresh milk, homemade curd (Dahi), eggs, paneer.
caregiver.nutri4: Antioxidants: Turmeric (Haldi) with warm milk, amla, tomatoes, carrots.
caregiver.nutri5: Hydration: Drink 8-10 glasses of clean water daily. Avoid excess strong chai or alcohol.
caregiver.phqDesc: Over the past 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by any of the following problems?
caregiver.phqQ1: 1. Little interest or pleasure in doing things

emergency.title: आपातकालीन चेतावनी संकेत (रेड फ्लैग)
emergency.subtitle: When to seek urgent and immediate emergency medical care
emergency.strokeDesc: Stroke is a medical emergency. Use FAST to identify symptoms immediately:
emergency.faceQ: FACE: Ask the person to smile. Does one side of the face droop?
emergency.armsQ: ARMS: Ask them to raise both arms. Does one arm drift downward?
emergency.speechQ: SPEECH: Ask them to repeat a simple phrase. Is speech slurred or strange?
emergency.timeQ: TIME: If ANY of these are YES — this is an emergency. Call 108 NOW.
emergency.inst1: Note the exact time symptoms started — tell the doctor immediately
emergency.inst2: Do NOT give food or water (choking risk)
emergency.inst3: Do NOT give aspirin unless specifically instructed by a doctor
emergency.inst4: Lay the person on their side if they feel sick or vomit
emergency.inst5: Keep them calm, warm, and still until the ambulance arrives
emergency.goldenHour: Golden Hour: Emergency intervention within 4.5 hours can prevent permanent brain damage.
emergency.strokeNormal: No stroke warning signs reported currently. Stay watchful. If any sign appears, return to this screen immediately.
emergency.seizureEmergTitle: ⚡ When a Seizure Needs Emergency Care
emergency.seizureEmergDesc: Most seizures end on their own. Call 108 immediately if any of these occur:
emergency.seizCrit2: Person does not wake up after the seizure
emergency.seizCrit3: A second seizure follows quickly without regaining consciousness
emergency.seizCrit4: Person is injured, in water, or pregnant
emergency.seizCrit5: This is their FIRST seizure ever
emergency.seizCrit6: Person has difficulty breathing or blue lips after the seizure
emergency.seizureFirstAidTitle: SEIZURE FIRST AID — What to do RIGHT NOW
emergency.do1: Clear the area of sharp or hard objects
emergency.do2: Place something soft (cloth/pillow) under their head
emergency.do3: Turn them gently onto their side (recovery position)
emergency.do4: Time the seizure with a watch or phone
emergency.do5: Stay with them reassuringly until fully awake
emergency.dont1: Do NOT put anything in their mouth (no spoons, keys, water)
emergency.dont2: Do NOT hold them down or restrain their movements
emergency.dont3: Do NOT give water, food, or medicines until fully awake
emergency.dont4: Do NOT panic — most seizures stop within 1 to 3 minutes
emergency.msRelapseTitle: 🔶 Signs of an MS Relapse — When to Contact Your Doctor
emergency.msRelapseDesc: A relapse refers to new symptoms or significant worsening of existing symptoms lasting more than 24 hours without fever:
emergency.msSign1: New numbness or tingling lasting more than 24 hours
emergency.msSign2: Sudden vision problems — blurring, double vision, or eye pain
emergency.msSign3: Severe new weakness in legs or arms making walking difficult
emergency.msSign4: Loss of balance or inability to walk that is new
emergency.msSign5: Bladder problems that are sudden and new
emergency.msRelapseMsg: Contact your neurologist or Primary Health Centre doctor promptly.
emergency.dangerDesc: Proceed to the nearest emergency department if you experience:
emergency.danger1: Sudden severe headache (worst headache of your life)
emergency.danger2: Sudden confusion or inability to understand speech
emergency.danger3: Sudden loss of vision in one or both eyes
emergency.danger4: Sudden weakness or numbness on one side of the body

clinicalScales.title: नैदानिक कार्यात्मक मापदंड

clinicalScales.mrsDesc: Measures degree of daily disability or dependence after stroke (0 = No symptoms, 5 = Severe disability):
clinicalScales.mrs0: 0 — No problems at all. I can do everything I did before stroke.
clinicalScales.mrs1: 1 — Minor difficulties, but I can do all my usual activities without help.
clinicalScales.mrs2: 2 — I cannot do some prior activities, but look after myself independently.
clinicalScales.mrs3: 3 — I need some assistance, but I am able to walk without another person.
clinicalScales.mrs4: 4 — I cannot walk or attend to body care needs without assistance.
clinicalScales.mrs5: 5 — Bedridden, incontinent, and requiring constant nursing care.
clinicalScales.edssDesc: Evaluates 6 functional domains on a 1 (severe difficulty) to 5 (normal) scale:
clinicalScales.seizQ1: How much do seizures affect your ability to work, study, or farm?

caregiver.subtitle: Practical training, emergency guidance, home rehabilitation, and nutrition
caregiver.rehabStroke1: Hand Ball Squeezes: Squeeze a soft rubber ball 10 times with each hand, 3 sets daily.
caregiver.rehabStroke2: Supported Arm Raises: Slowly lift both arms overhead for 5 seconds. Repeat 10 times.
caregiver.rehabStroke3: Ankle Circles: Rotate ankles in circles 10 times each direction while seated.
caregiver.rehabStroke4: Chair Sit-to-Stand: Stand up slowly without pulling, pause, and sit down gently. 5-10 times.
caregiver.rehabStroke5: Guided Walking: Walk slowly with a cane or family support, aiming for small daily increases.
caregiver.rehabMsTitle: Safe Daily Movement for Multiple Sclerosis
caregiver.rehabMs1: Gentle Stretching: Full-body stretching 5-10 minutes each morning to reduce stiffness.
caregiver.rehabMs2: Wall-Supported Balance: Stand near a sturdy wall; raise one foot for 10 seconds. Switch sides.
caregiver.rehabMs3: Cooling Precautions: Exercise in ventilated cool areas. Stop if feeling overheated.
caregiver.rehabMs4: Energy Pacing: Rest proactively. Do not push through severe neurological fatigue.
caregiver.rehabEpilepsy1: Consistent Sleep Schedule: Go to bed and wake up at consistent times every day.
caregiver.rehabEpilepsy2: Stress Reduction: 5 minutes of slow diaphragmatic breathing when feeling overwhelmed.
caregiver.rehabEpilepsy3: Exercise with a Buddy: Exercise with family nearby; avoid swimming or climbing alone.
caregiver.nutri1: Omega-3 Healthy Fats: Flaxseeds (Alsi) ground in roti, mustard oil in cooking, walnuts (akhrot).
caregiver.nutri2: Iron & Energy: Spinach (Palak), Jaggery (Gur), Ragi porridge, dates (Khajoor).
caregiver.nutri3: Nerve Health (B12): Fresh milk, homemade curd (Dahi), eggs, paneer.
caregiver.nutri4: Antioxidants: Turmeric (Haldi) with warm milk, amla, tomatoes, carrots.
caregiver.nutri5: Hydration: Drink 8-10 glasses of clean water daily. Avoid excess strong chai or alcohol.
caregiver.phqDesc: Over the past 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by any of the following problems?
caregiver.phqQ1: 1. Little interest or pleasure in doing things

emergency.title: आपातकालीन चेतावनी संकेत (रेड फ्लैग)
emergency.subtitle: When to seek urgent and immediate emergency medical care
emergency.strokeDesc: Stroke is a medical emergency. Use FAST to identify symptoms immediately:
emergency.faceQ: FACE: Ask the person to smile. Does one side of the face droop?
emergency.armsQ: ARMS: Ask them to raise both arms. Does one arm drift downward?
emergency.speechQ: SPEECH: Ask them to repeat a simple phrase. Is speech slurred or strange?
emergency.timeQ: TIME: If ANY of these are YES — this is an emergency. Call 108 NOW.
emergency.inst1: Note the exact time symptoms started — tell the doctor immediately
emergency.inst2: Do NOT give food or water (choking risk)
emergency.inst3: Do NOT give aspirin unless specifically instructed by a doctor
emergency.inst4: Lay the person on their side if they feel sick or vomit
emergency.inst5: Keep them calm, warm, and still until the ambulance arrives
emergency.goldenHour: Golden Hour: Emergency intervention within 4.5 hours can prevent permanent brain damage.
emergency.strokeNormal: No stroke warning signs reported currently. Stay watchful. If any sign appears, return to this screen immediately.
emergency.seizureEmergTitle: ⚡ When a Seizure Needs Emergency Care
emergency.seizureEmergDesc: Most seizures end on their own. Call 108 immediately if any of these occur:
emergency.seizCrit2: Person does not wake up after the seizure
emergency.seizCrit3: A second seizure follows quickly without regaining consciousness
emergency.seizCrit4: Person is injured, in water, or pregnant
emergency.seizCrit5: This is their FIRST seizure ever
emergency.seizCrit6: Person has difficulty breathing or blue lips after the seizure
emergency.seizureFirstAidTitle: SEIZURE FIRST AID — What to do RIGHT NOW
emergency.do1: Clear the area of sharp or hard objects
emergency.do2: Place something soft (cloth/pillow) under their head
emergency.do3: Turn them gently onto their side (recovery position)
emergency.do4: Time the seizure with a watch or phone
emergency.do5: Stay with them reassuringly until fully awake
emergency.dont1: Do NOT put anything in their mouth (no spoons, keys, water)
emergency.dont2: Do NOT hold them down or restrain their movements
emergency.dont3: Do NOT give water, food, or medicines until fully awake
emergency.dont4: Do NOT panic — most seizures stop within 1 to 3 minutes
emergency.msRelapseTitle: 🔶 Signs of an MS Relapse — When to Contact Your Doctor
emergency.msRelapseDesc: A relapse refers to new symptoms or significant worsening of existing symptoms lasting more than 24 hours without fever:
emergency.msSign1: New numbness or tingling lasting more than 24 hours
emergency.msSign2: Sudden vision problems — blurring, double vision, or eye pain
emergency.msSign3: Severe new weakness in legs or arms making walking difficult
emergency.msSign4: Loss of balance or inability to walk that is new
emergency.msSign5: Bladder problems that are sudden and new
emergency.msRelapseMsg: Contact your neurologist or Primary Health Centre doctor promptly.
emergency.dangerDesc: Proceed to the nearest emergency department if you experience:
emergency.danger1: Sudden severe headache (worst headache of your life)
emergency.danger2: Sudden confusion or inability to understand speech
emergency.danger3: Sudden loss of vision in one or both eyes
emergency.danger4: Sudden weakness or numbness on one side of the body

clinicalScales.title: नैदानिक कार्यात्मक मापदंड
clinicalScales.subtitle: Standardized clinician-aligned functional evaluations for longitudinal monitoring
clinicalScales.mrsDesc: Measures degree of daily disability or dependence after stroke (0 = No symptoms, 5 = Severe disability):
clinicalScales.mrs0: 0 — No problems at all. I can do everything I did before stroke.
clinicalScales.mrs1: 1 — Minor difficulties, but I can do all my usual activities without help.
clinicalScales.mrs2: 2 — I cannot do some prior activities, but look after myself independently.
clinicalScales.mrs3: 3 — I need some assistance, but I am able to walk without another person.
clinicalScales.mrs4: 4 — I cannot walk or attend to body care needs without assistance.
clinicalScales.mrs5: 5 — Bedridden, incontinent, and requiring constant nursing care.
clinicalScales.edssDesc: Evaluates 6 functional domains on a 1 (severe difficulty) to 5 (normal) scale:
clinicalScales.seizQ1: How much do seizures affect your ability to work, study, or farm?
clinicalScales.seizQ2: How much do seizures affect your social life and community interactions?
clinicalScales.seizQ3: How worried are you about having a seizure in public places?

caregiver.title: देखभालकर्ता एवं परिवार मार्गदर्शिका
caregiver.subtitle: Practical training, emergency guidance, home rehabilitation, and nutrition
caregiver.rehabStroke1: Hand Ball Squeezes: Squeeze a soft rubber ball 10 times with each hand, 3 sets daily.
caregiver.rehabStroke2: Supported Arm Raises: Slowly lift both arms overhead for 5 seconds. Repeat 10 times.
caregiver.rehabStroke3: Ankle Circles: Rotate ankles in circles 10 times each direction while seated.
caregiver.rehabStroke4: Chair Sit-to-Stand: Stand up slowly without pulling, pause, and sit down gently. 5-10 times.
caregiver.rehabStroke5: Guided Walking: Walk slowly with a cane or family support, aiming for small daily increases.
caregiver.rehabMsTitle: Safe Daily Movement for Multiple Sclerosis
caregiver.rehabMs1: Gentle Stretching: Full-body stretching 5-10 minutes each morning to reduce stiffness.
caregiver.rehabMs2: Wall-Supported Balance: Stand near a sturdy wall; raise one foot for 10 seconds. Switch sides.
caregiver.rehabMs3: Cooling Precautions: Exercise in ventilated cool areas. Stop if feeling overheated.
caregiver.rehabMs4: Energy Pacing: Rest proactively. Do not push through severe neurological fatigue.
caregiver.rehabEpilepsy1: Consistent Sleep Schedule: Go to bed and wake up at consistent times every day.
caregiver.rehabEpilepsy2: Stress Reduction: 5 minutes of slow diaphragmatic breathing when feeling overwhelmed.
caregiver.rehabEpilepsy3: Exercise with a Buddy: Exercise with family nearby; avoid swimming or climbing alone.
caregiver.nutri1: Omega-3 Healthy Fats: Flaxseeds (Alsi) ground in roti, mustard oil in cooking, walnuts (akhrot).
caregiver.nutri2: Iron & Energy: Spinach (Palak), Jaggery (Gur), Ragi porridge, dates (Khajoor).
caregiver.nutri3: Nerve Health (B12): Fresh milk, homemade curd (Dahi), eggs, paneer.
caregiver.nutri4: Antioxidants: Turmeric (Haldi) with warm milk, amla, tomatoes, carrots.
caregiver.nutri5: Hydration: Drink 8-10 glasses of clean water daily. Avoid excess strong chai or alcohol.
caregiver.phqDesc: Over the past 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by any of the following problems?
caregiver.phqQ1: 1. Little interest or pleasure in doing things

emergency.title: आपातकालीन चेतावनी संकेत (रेड फ्लैग)
emergency.subtitle: When to seek urgent and immediate emergency medical care
emergency.strokeDesc: Stroke is a medical emergency. Use FAST to identify symptoms immediately:
emergency.faceQ: FACE: Ask the person to smile. Does one side of the face droop?
emergency.armsQ: ARMS: Ask them to raise both arms. Does one arm drift downward?
emergency.speechQ: SPEECH: Ask them to repeat a simple phrase. Is speech slurred or strange?
emergency.timeQ: TIME: If ANY of these are YES — this is an emergency. Call 108 NOW.
emergency.inst1: Note the exact time symptoms started — tell the doctor immediately
emergency.inst2: Do NOT give food or water (choking risk)
emergency.inst3: Do NOT give aspirin unless specifically instructed by a doctor
emergency.inst4: Lay the person on their side if they feel sick or vomit
emergency.inst5: Keep them calm, warm, and still until the ambulance arrives
emergency.goldenHour: Golden Hour: Emergency intervention within 4.5 hours can prevent permanent brain damage.
emergency.strokeNormal: No stroke warning signs reported currently. Stay watchful. If any sign appears, return to this screen immediately.
emergency.seizureEmergTitle: ⚡ When a Seizure Needs Emergency Care
emergency.seizureEmergDesc: Most seizures end on their own. Call 108 immediately if any of these occur:
emergency.seizCrit2: Person does not wake up after the seizure
emergency.seizCrit3: A second seizure follows quickly without regaining consciousness
emergency.seizCrit4: Person is injured, in water, or pregnant
emergency.seizCrit5: This is their FIRST seizure ever
emergency.seizCrit6: Person has difficulty breathing or blue lips after the seizure
emergency.seizureFirstAidTitle: SEIZURE FIRST AID — What to do RIGHT NOW
emergency.do1: Clear the area of sharp or hard objects
emergency.do2: Place something soft (cloth/pillow) under their head
emergency.do3: Turn them gently onto their side (recovery position)
emergency.do4: Time the seizure with a watch or phone
emergency.do5: Stay with them reassuringly until fully awake
emergency.dont1: Do NOT put anything in their mouth (no spoons, keys, water)
emergency.dont2: Do NOT hold them down or restrain their movements
emergency.dont3: Do NOT give water, food, or medicines until fully awake
emergency.dont4: Do NOT panic — most seizures stop within 1 to 3 minutes
emergency.msRelapseTitle: 🔶 Signs of an MS Relapse — When to Contact Your Doctor
emergency.msRelapseDesc: A relapse refers to new symptoms or significant worsening of existing symptoms lasting more than 24 hours without fever:
emergency.msSign1: New numbness or tingling lasting more than 24 hours
emergency.msSign2: Sudden vision problems — blurring, double vision, or eye pain
emergency.msSign3: Severe new weakness in legs or arms making walking difficult
emergency.msSign4: Loss of balance or inability to walk that is new
emergency.msSign5: Bladder problems that are sudden and new
emergency.msRelapseMsg: Contact your neurologist or Primary Health Centre doctor promptly.
emergency.dangerDesc: Proceed to the nearest emergency department if you experience:
emergency.danger1: Sudden severe headache (worst headache of your life)
emergency.danger2: Sudden confusion or inability to understand speech
emergency.danger3: Sudden loss of vision in one or both eyes
emergency.danger4: Sudden weakness or numbness on one side of the body

clinicalScales.title: नैदानिक कार्यात्मक मापदंड
clinicalScales.subtitle: Standardized clinician-aligned functional evaluations for longitudinal monitoring
clinicalScales.mrsDesc: Measures degree of daily disability or dependence after stroke (0 = No symptoms, 5 = Severe disability):
clinicalScales.mrs0: 0 — No problems at all. I can do everything I did before stroke.
clinicalScales.mrs1: 1 — Minor difficulties, but I can do all my usual activities without help.
clinicalScales.mrs2: 2 — I cannot do some prior activities, but look after myself independently.
clinicalScales.mrs3: 3 — I need some assistance, but I am able to walk without another person.
clinicalScales.mrs4: 4 — I cannot walk or attend to body care needs without assistance.
clinicalScales.mrs5: 5 — Bedridden, incontinent, and requiring constant nursing care.
clinicalScales.edssDesc: Evaluates 6 functional domains on a 1 (severe difficulty) to 5 (normal) scale:
clinicalScales.seizQ1: How much do seizures affect your ability to work, study, or farm?
clinicalScales.seizQ2: How much do seizures affect your social life and community interactions?
clinicalScales.seizQ3: How worried are you about having a seizure in public places?
clinicalScales.seizQ4: How well controlled do you feel your seizures are on current medicines?
clinicalScales.seizQ5: How much do medicine side effects affect your everyday wellbeing?
clinicalScales.adlTitle: Activities of Daily Living (ADL) Independence Check
clinicalScales.adlDesc: Can you perform these 8 essential daily activities independently?
clinicalScales.adl8: Using a mobile phone or communicating

caregiver.title: देखभालकर्ता एवं परिवार मार्गदर्शिका
caregiver.subtitle: Practical training, emergency guidance, home rehabilitation, and nutrition
caregiver.rehabStroke1: Hand Ball Squeezes: Squeeze a soft rubber ball 10 times with each hand, 3 sets daily.
caregiver.rehabStroke2: Supported Arm Raises: Slowly lift both arms overhead for 5 seconds. Repeat 10 times.
caregiver.rehabStroke3: Ankle Circles: Rotate ankles in circles 10 times each direction while seated.
caregiver.rehabStroke4: Chair Sit-to-Stand: Stand up slowly without pulling, pause, and sit down gently. 5-10 times.
caregiver.rehabStroke5: Guided Walking: Walk slowly with a cane or family support, aiming for small daily increases.
caregiver.rehabMsTitle: Safe Daily Movement for Multiple Sclerosis
caregiver.rehabMs1: Gentle Stretching: Full-body stretching 5-10 minutes each morning to reduce stiffness.
caregiver.rehabMs2: Wall-Supported Balance: Stand near a sturdy wall; raise one foot for 10 seconds. Switch sides.
caregiver.rehabMs3: Cooling Precautions: Exercise in ventilated cool areas. Stop if feeling overheated.
caregiver.rehabMs4: Energy Pacing: Rest proactively. Do not push through severe neurological fatigue.
caregiver.rehabEpilepsy1: Consistent Sleep Schedule: Go to bed and wake up at consistent times every day.
caregiver.rehabEpilepsy2: Stress Reduction: 5 minutes of slow diaphragmatic breathing when feeling overwhelmed.
caregiver.rehabEpilepsy3: Exercise with a Buddy: Exercise with family nearby; avoid swimming or climbing alone.
caregiver.nutri1: Omega-3 Healthy Fats: Flaxseeds (Alsi) ground in roti, mustard oil in cooking, walnuts (akhrot).
caregiver.nutri2: Iron & Energy: Spinach (Palak), Jaggery (Gur), Ragi porridge, dates (Khajoor).
caregiver.nutri3: Nerve Health (B12): Fresh milk, homemade curd (Dahi), eggs, paneer.
caregiver.nutri4: Antioxidants: Turmeric (Haldi) with warm milk, amla, tomatoes, carrots.
caregiver.nutri5: Hydration: Drink 8-10 glasses of clean water daily. Avoid excess strong chai or alcohol.
caregiver.phqDesc: Over the past 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by any of the following problems?
caregiver.phqQ1: 1. Little interest or pleasure in doing things
caregiver.phqPositive: Your responses suggest you may benefit from speaking with a counselor. This is common and treatable. Please call Tele-MANAS (14416) or talk to your doctor.
caregiver.phqNegative: Screening score is within the normal range. Continue regular wellness practices.
caregiver.burnoutMsg: Caregiver exhaustion is real and important. You cannot care for a loved one if your own health suffers. Take scheduled rest periods, share chores with relatives, and speak with your ASHA worker.
